extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of communication, media studies, and cultural studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting interpretive, cultural-science analyses of mass communication: how to study media as symbolic texts, what to attend to (meaning, voice, context, technology), and what methodological moves to avoid (reduction to functions or causal antecedents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive goal — diagnose meanings not predict behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: “Cultural studies does not attempt to predict human behavior; rather, it attempts to diagnose human meanings.” (Carey: cultural studies has more modest objectives than predictive or causal models.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to explicate the meanings people place on experience (explication), building readable accounts of what people say and do instead of producing lawlike predictive statements. The objective is to enlarge the human conversation by comprehending others' answers rather than to generate universal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verstehen — decipher public interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use verstehen: an attempt to decipher the interpretations people cast on their experience, interpretations available out in the public world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and interpret observable public expressions (conversation, ritual, behavior) to recover actors' own meanings. This is not 'mind-reading' but constructing interpretations from available social signs; e.g., analyze how different groups define death in socially meaningful ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat human action as text — construct a reading
rubrics_metrics.description: View human action—or more accurately human action—as a text. 'Our task is to construct a “reading” of the text.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach speech, gestures, rituals, and practices as ensembles of symbols to be read much like literary texts. Expect fragmentary, ambiguous, and context-dependent data; construct coherent interpretive readings that make the meanings explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to symbolic processes and the voice/content of cultural forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay serious attention to the autonomous process of symbolic formation; examine the content and the 'voice in which films speak.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore the concrete content of experiences (images, voices, narratives). Analyze how symbolic devices operate to produce meanings (tone, voice, imagery) rather than only inferring functions or motives from behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid functionalist reductionism and over-reliance on latent functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional analysis tends to invoke latent functions and to move from causes to consequences without inspecting the symbolic system; such analyses 'remain hopelessly equivocal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reduce cultural phenomena solely to their purported social functions (e.g., solidarity, anxiety relief). Treat latent-function explanations with caution and interrogate how meanings and symbols produce effects rather than assuming a priori function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid simple antecedent-causality models for explaining culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictive models that link antecedent exposure or social-structural variables (race, class, income) to cultural outcomes usually explain only a minuscule amount of variation and force antiessentialism on the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be skeptical of attempts to explain cultural meanings or practices purely by antecedent variables. Recognize limits of correlational/causal models and prefer richer interpretive accounts when addressing cultural forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize interpretations within history, technology, and social structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Advances in understanding culture cannot be secured unless they are tied to a vivid sense of technology and social structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link readings of texts and cultural forms to their historical circumstances and the material/technological means of communication; analyze how technologies and institutional contexts shape forms of expression and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume multiple realities and avoid privileging scientific frames
rubrics_metrics.description: Start from the assumption of multiple realities; do not grade experience into zones of epistemological correctness (scientific vs. aesthetic vs. religious).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that people inhabit qualitatively distinct zones of experience organized by different symbolic frames. Avoid the conceit that scientific modes are inherently superior; study each frame on its own terms and compare reciprocally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a theory of fictions / semiotics to explain cultural forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a 'theory of fictions'—a theory explaining how cultural forms operate, the semantic devices they employ, the meanings they sustain, and the particular glow they cast over experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work toward explanatory frameworks (semiotics, semantics) that account for how symbolic forms construct realities. This involves specifying the devices and operations through which forms (art, journalism, ideology, religion) shape meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize particularity and resist universalizing claims about human minds
rubrics_metrics.description: There are enough particular individuals and particular scenes to make doctrines that posit changeless universal structures of mind seem 'merely quaint.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on detailed, situated analyses of specific scenes, practices, and histories rather than attempting to infer sweeping universal cognitive structures; emphasize historical and cultural particularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use content analysis but tie it to semantic theory rather than only needs/functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Content analyses are often referred backward to needs or forward to social systems they maintain; instead they should be connected to theories of meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conducting content analyses, interpret content via semantic or semiotic frameworks rather than reducing it solely to reflections of needs, motives, or system-maintenance functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze multiple cultural worlds and their interpenetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the several cultural worlds in which people simultaneously exist—the tension between them, patterns of mood and motivation distinctive to each, and the interpenetration among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how different cultural spheres (popular art, science, religion, ordinary speech) produce distinct moods and motives and how they sometimes interrelate or conflict. Assess the reach and limits of effects across these worlds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt modest scholarly aims — make available others' answers and build veridical records
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of cultural studies is 'to make available to us answers that others... have given and thus to include them in the consumable record of what man has said.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to produce faithful, comprehensible accounts of cultural meanings that make others' interpretations accessible. The task is not to impose meanings but to record and interpret culturally situated answers.
